result.note: Tests the Semicon 2.0 approval and the 2021 mission's record, the mobile-phone incentive design, and India's electronics manufacturing data.

questions.prompt: In July 2026, the Union Cabinet approved Semicon 2.0. Consider the following statements:
items: Semicon 2.0 has an outlay of USD 13.3 billion (INR 1.275 trillion) and covers chip design, equipment, materials, fabrication, packaging, research and skills.
The 2021 semiconductor mission approved 12 manufacturing units and 24 design projects.
No facility approved under the 2021 semiconductor mission had begun commercial production by July 2026.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 3 is wrong because three facilities under the 2021 mission are already producing commercially. Semicon 2.0 shifts the focus from landing factories to building the ecosystem around them.
questions.source: The 2021 semiconductor mission has approved 12 manufacturing units and 24 design projects; three facilities are already producing commercially.

questions.prompt: In July 2026, the Union Cabinet approved USD 6.5 billion over five years for mobile-phone manufacturing. What base incentive can firms receive under it, before any extra for local sourcing?
questions.explain: Firms can receive 2.25%–5% of eligible sales, plus up to 1.5% for sourcing key components locally. TBB notes that pairing phone incentives with chip subsidies builds demand alongside supply.
questions.source: Firms can receive 2.25%–5% of eligible sales, plus up to 1.5% for sourcing key components locally.

questions.prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to India's electronics sector, as reported in July 2026:
items: India's global rank in mobile-phone manufacturing — Second
Mobile-phone exports in FY2024–25 — USD 20.9 billion
questions.ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explain: The third pair is wrong because domestic value addition across electronics remains just 18%–20%. India is the world's second-largest mobile-phone manufacturer, with production of USD 56.9 billion in FY2024–25.
questions.source: Domestic value addition across electronics remains just 18%–20%.
